cards.explanation: The answer is False. God says, “…I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people…” (Exodus 33:3). He does say He will send an angel before them, but He Himself won't be going along. I think that line landed hard on everyone who heard it.

The answer is destroy. God says He won't go with them “otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.” (Exodus 33:3). A few verses later He says it again: “If I should go with you for a single moment, I would destroy you.” (Exodus 33:5). He says it twice, friends, so it's clearly worth catching.

The answer is jewelry. The verse says “…no one put on any of his jewelry.” (Exodus 33:4). The people had just heard the bad news, and they went into mourning. Then verse 6 says the Israelites stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.

The answer is that He would decide what to do with them. The LORD says, “Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.” (Exodus 33:5). He doesn't say what He'll decide yet. We just have to wait and see, so keep reading, bakers.

The answer is anyone inquiring of the LORD. The text says, “…anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.” (Exodus 33:7). Anyone. The tent isn't kept for a short list of important names. If you wanted to ask the LORD something, you walked out there.

The answer is that the LORD speaks with Moses. “As Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance, and the LORD would speak with Moses.” (Exodus 33:9). The cloud settles at the door, and then the LORD speaks. Verse 7 says anyone inquiring of the LORD would go to this tent outside the camp. Moses walks in, and he isn't left standing there wondering.

The answer is True. “When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they would stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.” (Exodus 33:10). They didn't have to walk to the tent. Verse 8 says they would stand at their own tent entrances and watch Moses until he went in, so they were already right there. Front row seats, friends, and nobody had to fight for parking.

The answer is face to face like a friend. “Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend.” (Exodus 33:11). That line is the heart of the scene. It's like two friends talking across the counter, with nobody in between. Right after it, Moses speaks to the LORD (Exodus 33:12), and the LORD answers him (Exodus 33:14).

The answer is Joshua. “…his young assistant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.” (Exodus 33:11). Moses heads back to camp, but Joshua stays put in the tent. The text doesn't say why he stayed, and I'd love to know. I bet I would have stayed too, wouldn't you, friends?

The answer is True. Moses says, “Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have found favor in My sight.’” (Exodus 33:12). Moses is reminding the LORD of what He already told him. Being known by name is a good thing to bring up.

The answer is True. Moses says, “…please let me know Your ways, that I may know You and find favor in Your sight.” (Exodus 33:13). Moses is asking to know the LORD better, and that's a good thing to ask for. Then he adds, “Remember that this nation is Your people.” (Exodus 33:13). He asks for himself, and then he speaks up for the people.

The answer is that His Presence will go and give rest. The LORD answers, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” (Exodus 33:14). Back in verse 3 He had said He would not go with them. Here He speaks of His own Presence going, and of rest. After all that bad news, rest is a nice word to hear, bakers.

The answer is that they have found favor in His sight. Moses asks, “For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight, unless You go with us?” (Exodus 33:16). Moses isn't asking for a trophy or a parade. He wants the proof of God's favor to be God Himself walking with them. If you've ever wanted the real thing and not just a nice sticker on the box, you get Moses here.

The answer is True. Moses asks, “How else will we be distinguished from all the other people on the face of the earth?” (Exodus 33:16). In his words, God going with them is what sets them apart from every other people. Think of a batch where one cookie is the only one stamped by the master, friends. Everybody can tell which one it is.

The answer is glory. Moses says, “Please show me Your glory.” (Exodus 33:18). The LORD had just said yes to his last request in verse 17, and Moses asks for more. I'd have been nervous asking again, but Moses just asks it plainly.

The answer is His name, the LORD. Moses asked to see the LORD's glory, and the LORD answers by saying what He will do. First, “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you…” (Exodus 33:19). Then He says He will proclaim His name, the LORD, with Moses standing right there to hear it.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). He also says later, “…My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). So Moses is told he can't see His face.

The answer is that no one can see Him and live. The LORD says, “You cannot see My face, for no one can see Me and live.” (Exodus 33:20). That's the reason He gives, and it's a serious one. He doesn't say no and leave it there, though. In the next verses He tells Moses where to stand on a rock and what He will do (Exodus 33:21, 22, 23).

The answer is that He will put Moses in the rock and cover him with His hand. The LORD says, “…I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.” (Exodus 33:22). A cleft is a crack in the rock. I think that sounds like a safe spot, friends, with the LORD's own hand over you.

The answer is back. The LORD says, “Then I will take My hand away, and you will see My back; but My face must not be seen.” (Exodus 33:23). Before that, He says He will put Moses in a cleft of the rock and cover him with His hand until He has passed by (Exodus 33:22). So Moses gets covered first, then he sees. I think if I were standing in that rock, I'd be holding very, very still.
